question.worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[4]{\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{(2{x}^{2}+1)^{8}}} \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{(2{x}^{2}+1)^{8}}]}^{1/4} \\  & =({x}^{2}+4)^{1/4}(2{x}^{2}+1)^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+4)^{1/4}(2{x}^{2}+1)^{-2}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+4)^{1/4})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((2{x}^{2}+1)^{-2}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}+1)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\cdot (2x)-2\cdot \frac{1}{2{x}^{2}+1}\cdot (4x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{x}{2({x}^{2}+4)}-\frac{8x}{2{x}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{16x}{2{x}^{2}+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{y}{2}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{16x}{2{x}^{2}+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\sqrt[4]{\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{(2{x}^{2}+1)^{8}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt[4]{\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{(2{x}^{2}+1)^{8}}}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{16x}{2{x}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{1/4}}{2(2{x}^{2}+1)^{2}}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{16x}{2{x}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{1/4}}{2(2{x}^{2}+1)^{2}}(\frac{x(2{x}^{2}+1)-16x({x}^{2}+4)}{({x}^{2}+4)(2{x}^{2}+1)}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{1/4}}{2(2{x}^{2}+1)^{2}}(\frac{-14{x}^{3}-63x}{({x}^{2}+4)(2{x}^{2}+1)}) \\  & =-\frac{x(14{x}^{2}+63)}{2(2{x}^{2}+1)^{3}\sqrt[4]{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
